description: agent-hierarchy — SessionStart injects the resolved role→model table and the orchestration protocol on startup, resume, clear, fork, and post-compaction (so it survives compaction). It classifies the session three ways: a subagent (agent_id set) gets nothing, which is the intent here, since role agents carry their own instructions in agents/*.md and an Implementor that starts orchestrating would defeat the hierarchy; a top-level `claude --agent <hierarchy role>` session gets a short notice that it is NOT the Orchestrator; everything else gets the ordinary directive. The discriminator is agent_id, not agent_type — a top-level --agent session sets agent_type too, so testing it misclassifies a genuine main session as a subagent. Silent when the config sets enabled:false; with no config at all it emits a one-line nudge to run /hierarchy init. PreToolUse runs the ultra gate on Agent/Task/SendMessage: it holds Ultra-Advisor escalation for the user, whether dispatched as a subagent or via SendMessage to its named peer session — the first dispatch of each session is denied with instructions to put the decision to the user and record their answer (allow this session / ask each time / blocked this session) via hooks/gate.mjs; the answer is session-scoped and lives in ~/.claude/agent-hierarchy.gate.json. Every other tool call, and every SendMessage not addressed to the Ultra-Advisor's peer, passes through untouched. SubagentStop runs the usage collector: it sums the finished subagent's transcript (token counts the harness already logged) into ~/.claude/agent-hierarchy.usage.jsonl — plain node, zero model cost — which /hierarchy usage or hooks/usage-report.mjs renders as session/day/week/month reports. UserPromptSubmit also tracks the peer report-back contract: a delivered prompt carrying a `[hierarchy-peer-brief reply-to="..." task="..."]` sentinel inside its `<cross-session-message>` wrapper records a pending obligation in ~/.claude/agent-hierarchy.peer-pending.jsonl. PostToolUse (matcher SendMessage) resolves that obligation once a reply is sent to the recorded address, its name, or an explicit third-party reply-to. Stop blocks the session's turn from ending while an obligation is still owed, nudging at most twice before waiving it and allowing the stop regardless — fail-open throughout, and inert for subagents, exactly like the other hooks above. Enforcement arms only on a peer-delivered turn: UserPromptSubmit also arms a per-session turn marker whenever a wrapped message (a brief, a ping, or anything else carrying the cross-session-message envelope) leaves a pending obligation behind, and Stop's nudge/waive logic runs only on an armed turn, disarming it afterward either way — so a user directly chatting with a tasked peer neither triggers a nudge nor spends one. Three more mechanisms since 0.29.0, all fail-open and inert for subagents. Message files: PreToolUse (same Agent|Task|SendMessage matcher, after the ultra gate) runs the msg gate — a role dispatch (Agent spawn of architect/implementor/reviewer/ultra-advisor, or a SendMessage carrying the peer-brief sentinel) must carry `[hierarchy-msg <abs request path>]` naming an existing request file under `<hierarchy dir>/msgs/` whose `to:` matches the role, else it is denied with the msg.mjs command to write one; SubagentStop runs the response nudge — a hierarchy role subagent briefed by file whose final message lacks `[hierarchy-msg <response path>]` is blocked ONCE (per agent_id, recorded in gates.jsonl) with instructions to write its response file; the peer-side resolver likewise requires the response pointer when the obligation was recorded with one. Peer roster: a top-level `--agent <role>` session appends `up` at SessionStart and `down` at SessionEnd (hooks/sessionend-roster.mjs) to `<hierarchy dir>/peers.jsonl`; PostToolUse on ListAgents|SendMessage (hooks/posttooluse-roster.mjs) records `seen` (parsed from the ListAgents listing, role-matching names only) and `briefed`; Route gate: PreToolUse (hooks/pretooluse-route-gate.mjs, third in the chain) keeps chain roles (Ultra-Advisor, Architect, Reviewer, Implementor, and custom chain roles) as peers: every Agent/Task dispatch of one from the Orchestrator is denied, every time, naming the live peer to SendMessage or carrying the exact spawn command. There is no route question and no opt-in. Legwork roles (task-runner, task-gopher, custom legwork roles) pass: they alone run as subagents. `ah:orchestrator` is never dispatched as a subagent, and role sessions and subagents never dispatch a chain role. Tier rule: the same route gate denies ONCE per session and role when the session model is known, the target is Architect or Ultra-Advisor at or below the session's tier, and the request file carries no `reason:` (with `msgs:"off"` the denial text drops the `reason:` instruction, since there is no request file to carry it). SessionStart appends a HIERARCHY STATE block (open exchanges, roster, tier line) on every matcher including compact, and sweeps closed exchanges older than 7 days on startup. `msgs:"off"` in agent-hierarchy.json disables the two message gates; the CLI and the state listing stay. Streams: hooks/stream-label.mjs runs on UserPromptSubmit, Stop and Notification (matcher permission_prompt) only in a roster-spawned herdr peer whose team row is tagged into an open stream, and re-renders that stream's tab glyph through `roster.mjs stream-label`, the same CLI that holds the other stream verbs (`stream-open`, `stream-status`, `stream-done`) and `--stream` on `spawn-one`/`spawn-ad-hoc`. Push guard: PreToolUse on Bash (hooks/pretooluse-push-guard.mjs, last on that matcher) writes nothing; its push rules act only in repos that commit `.claude/ah-conventions.json` on origin's default branch, read from that ref and never the working tree. There it denies force pushes, --no-verify, deletions, bulk and tag pushes, remotes other than origin, pushes to the default or a protected branch, pushes whose range touches a protected path, and remote-config writes — one calm systemMessage line for the user, an `ah-push-guard:<RULE>` reason for the model. Errors before opt-in is established allow; errors after it deny (PG-ERROR). Inert in every other repo. While a /pipeline run is open, in any repo, it also denies every way the run could merge, approve, ready or auto-merge a PR (PG-MERGE, PG-AUTOMERGE, PG-APPROVE, PG-READY, PG-API-MERGE), no git command among them, and if those checks throw on a merge form, or liveness is unknown, it denies (PG-MERGE-ERROR); the one exception, the pinned merge command from the top-level Orchestrator of a run that opted into auto-merge, gets the native permission prompt (otherwise PG-MERGE-ROLE or PG-MERGE). PostToolUse on Bash (hooks/posttooluse-merge-record.mjs) appends a merge line to the run's decision log when that command ran. PreToolUse on GitHub MCP tools (hooks/pretooluse-mcp-guard.mjs) denies, while a run is open, a tool that merges, approves, or readies a PR (PG-MCP-MERGE); tools from other servers exit at once. The activity hook (activity.mjs) records a Claude role session's own activity for the hierarchy status file: UserPromptSubmit working, Stop idle, a permission prompt blocked, and PostToolUse (async) working again; UserPromptSubmit and Stop also refresh status.json in any session with a hierarchy dir.
